Unknown Realm 18.note: roof mix probe, FIRST LAYOUT -- bays in a row along x with ridges along x too, so the gable verges faced each other and no square-on end elevation was possible. Superseded by Realm 21.

Unknown Realm 19.note: roof mix probe, ridges turned across the row. Read at long range and the eaves shadow was misread as an open gable on bays 2 and 3 -- see Realm 20.

Unknown Realm 20.note: THE USER'S OWN HAND-BUILD, two roofs on one 6x4 footprint. Pasted to settle whether the 'open gable' on Realm 19 was real: it is not, both hand-built verges are closed and the dark triangle was eaves shadow at distance. Ground truth for docs/roofscape.md 8.

Unknown Realm 21.note: roof mix probe, bay 2 rewired to drive the SHIPPED _lay_gabled_wing + gable_infill instead of a hand-rolled copy. THE READ: bay 3 (end-mix, the hand-build's technique) is the only one of three that reads as a gabled house; bay 1 (ours) is a flat-topped box; bay 2 (shipped flush gable) is a horizontal band with the roof set back. docs/roofscape.md 9.

Unknown Realm 22.note: roof mix probe with bay 3 driving the SHIPPED endmix treatment. The wired path reproduces the hand-build's gable; verges are symmetric 1-cell (4 x End 01) where the hand-build used 1-and-2 cells, which is gable_end_piece's deliberate choice -- see roof-end-wide-verge.

Unknown Realm 23.note: East Tradebourne crop 300,240,180,180 at seed 33 -- the first REAL town built with endmix. 180 square because quarters need a 1.2 clustering lift and a small crop has none (gable-ends); this one reads 1.28x. 384 Village Roof Side End 01, hip corners down to 8, 211 of 213 wings gabled.

Unknown Realm 24.note: East Tradebourne crop 300,240,180,180 rebuilt with the flat-top fix and the chimney split. Ridges instead of plateaus, and every stack a plain stone chimney on the ridge with no slope skirt. Seams 3,822 -> 1,526 against the etcrop build of the same crop.

Unknown Realm 5.note: market cross sweep, 4 shafts x 4 heads on 3 steps. Pinnacle-on-drum wins; steps read; null column proves the shaft works.

Unknown Realm 6.note: barn aisle posts, 4 treatments at a 20 ft eaves. Neither beam nor pillar survives; the blank tall wall reads as a fortress.
